historical_reviews.deepseek: Queries the relevant fields but neither authenticates the target nor proves the selected BDF is the intended link, and grep removes identity and status context.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires an approved device role, full verbose output, secure transport and no PCIe mutation.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Negotiated width and speed are meaningful only for the correct link endpoint or port and its current power/link state; LnkSta below LnkCap can be acceptable power management, designed lane bifurcation or a real down-training fault depending on the approved recipe.

original_test_intent: Verify that the intended PCIe link negotiates the speed and lane width required by the platform SPEC.
original_method: Authenticate the exact SUT, resolve an owner-approved domain-qualified BDF and physical device/port role, collect complete `lspci -s BDF -vvv` output with exit status, parse identity plus LnkCap and LnkSta, account for link state and policy, and compare negotiated speed/width to the approved recipe without reset, rescan or configuration writes.
manual_activity: A platform owner confirms the physical device/port, expected generation and lane allocation, and decides whether any negotiated-versus-capability difference is acceptable.
safety_requirements: Preserve complete verbose output and exit status
Do not rescan PCIe, retrain or reset the link/device, bind/unbind drivers or write configuration space
Stop on missing identity or link fields
agent_execution_scope: Parse device identity, LnkCap and LnkSta
Compare speed and width with the approved role-specific SPEC
Flag link-down, downgraded or ambiguous states
engineer_actions: Approve generation, width, bifurcation and power policy

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The lspci query is relevant, but insecure transport and grep-only evidence do not prove device identity or retain the context needed to interpret the link.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through verified-host SSH, capture complete read-only `lspci -s <domain:BDF> -vvv` output and exit status, then parse identity, LnkCap and LnkSta against an approved device-role SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The PCIE_BUS speed/width objective and 40-minute activity remain; authenticated identity and full-context comparison are added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve the physical role first, then record capability and negotiated generation/width with link-state and approved bifurcation/power-policy context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an unauthenticated grep excerpt with complete identity-bound evidence and explicit interpretation rules.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A correct-looking LnkSta line from the wrong BDF or a transient low-power state can falsely pass or fail the case.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BDFs can move across firmware/topology changes; resolve them through the approved inventory rather than guessing from a previous boot.

project_override_considerations: Define whether acceptance requires negotiated values equal to LnkCap or to a lower platform limit, how bifurcated links are represented, and whether low-power or link-down observations require a stable workload/state prerequisite.
expected_evidence: Verified target, host key and board/firmware identity
Approved BDF-to-physical-role mapping and SPEC revision
Complete lspci verbose output with exit status
Parsed identity, LnkCap and LnkSta speed/width and link state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request a PCIe speed/width comparison. DeepSeek's security, identity and evidence omissions are execution defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target role, BDF and expected link policy are identifiable inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED only if the physical mapping or authoritative speed/width expectation cannot be obtained.

review_improvement: Binds negotiated-link evidence to one authenticated physical PCIe role and distinguishes capability from the role-specific accepted operating state.
independent_technical_reasoning: LnkCap is the component's advertised maximum while LnkSta is the current negotiated result. Equality is not universally required: motherboard lane routing, bifurcation and power policy can impose an approved lower state, so an engineer-owned physical-role recipe is necessary before the agent can classify a difference.
